office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, including school funding, taxes, housing, and criminal statutes.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Jamila E. Taylor, chair of the House Civil Rights & Judiciary Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Tiffany Bowyer, a Federal Way small-business owner. The race splits on taxes, government spending, and public safety.

candidates.summary: Incumbent state representative and attorney who chairs the House Civil Rights & Judiciary Committee, running on gun-violence, police-training, housing, and tax-credit legislation.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million [S4]
Says excessive policing and incarceration should not be the community solution to crime rooted in systemic inequity [S2]
Voted for ESHB 1296 and ESSB 5599; endorsed by SEIU 775 and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S5][S7][S11][S12]

taxes.basis: Voted for the tax on income over $1 million; otherwise cites targeted small-business tax cuts and expanded working-family credits.

spending.basis: Runs on delivering public resources for housing and childcare and calls for free childcare options.

housing.basis: Cites delivering housing resources and pledges that every family can keep a roof over their head and access services.

safety.basis: Centers root causes of crime and says excessive policing and incarceration are not the solution, while citing police-training and trust legislation.

experience.basis: Sitting representative and committee chair with bills passed since 2021, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted for ESSB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended the Initiative 2081 parental-rights list; no separate statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and Federal Way small-business owner running on voting no on new taxes, independent audits of state programs, and full police staffing.
highlights: Pledges to vote no on new taxes that burden working families and small businesses [S2]
Calls for independent audits, transparent reporting, and performance standards for state programs [S2]
Supports fully staffing police and repeat-offender accountability alongside behavioral-health teams [S2]

taxes.basis: Pledges to vote no on new taxes and blames rising property taxes and fees on growing government spending.

spending.basis: Centers independent audits, performance standards, and government living within its means.

safety.basis: Prioritizes full police staffing and repeat-offender accountability, paired with behavioral-health teams.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience, running against an incumbent committee chair.
